cita: Yang et al. (2023). Failures Pave the Way: Enhancing Large Language Models through Tuning-free Rule Accumulation.
problema: Frozen (API-only, non-fine-tunable) LLMs deployed on streaming data keep repeating the same class of mistake because nothing persists across inputs, while existing prompt-optimization approaches assume a static training set rather than an unbounded online stream of tasks.
mecanismo: Tuning-free Rule Accumulation (TRAN): on each mistake the LLM generates candidate 'if...then...' rules, retests them and keeps only rules that actually fix the current error; if none work, the failed case is stored in a separate mistake collection and later retrieved (by similarity) to summarize a rule jointly from multiple related failures; a maintenance step uses the LLM itself to detect and discard redundant or contradictory incoming rules against the existing collection, and an LRU eviction policy caps the collection size; at inference, BM25 retrieves the top rules for the current input and prepends them to the base prompt.
evaluacion: Evaluated on BBQ-Lite (7 social-bias multi-choice tasks), TweetEval/AGNews/DBPedia text classification, and Dyck Language generation, in zero-shot and few-shot streaming settings, against Zero-Shot CoT, Auto-CoT and SALAM baselines, plus an ablation removing LRU / multi-mistake summarization / duplicate-contradiction checking, and out-of-domain rule-transfer and counterfactual-distribution-shift stress tests.
numeros_clave: Zero-shot BBQ-Lite average 91.6% (TRAN) vs 75.4% (frozen model) vs 82.8% (SALAM), +8.8pp over SALAM (Table 1); mistake-rate reduction of ~40% (zero-shot) / ~20% (few-shot) after 700 samples (Fig.3); ablation: removing multi-mistake summarization costs ~3pp average accuracy, removing the LRU cap costs up to 4.5pp on the Disability task (10/39/15 rules pruned per task, Table 4); out-of-domain rule transfer from Physical to SES task gives +10% accuracy (Fig.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The entire framework is built from observed mistakes only: a rule is admitted to the collection only after being tested and shown to fix the specific failure it was derived from (§2.3, process (b)) — direct support for MF's negative-knowledge stance that durable memory should be built from validated failures, not just accumulated observations.

Rule maintenance uses the LLM itself to detect near-duplicate/contradictory incoming rules against the existing collection and keep only the newest (§2.4), plus LRU eviction once a size threshold is crossed — measured to matter (ablation: removing LRU costs up to 4.5pp, Table 4) — a concrete self-managed pruning recipe MF could adopt.

Retrieval uses plain BM25 over the rule collection (top-3 of up to 100 rules) and the paper explicitly measures the value of summarizing across MULTIPLE related mistakes versus a single one (removing this costs performance, Table 4) rather than assuming richer retrieval helps — matches MF's measured-retrieval stance.

Rules are deliberately kept independent of, and composable with, the base prompt and other prompting strategies (CoT), shown to compose additively (+4.3 to +9.6pp when combined with CoT, Table 5) — a pattern of a single reusable knowledge store composing cleanly across surfaces, relevant to MF's single-source-per-fact stance.

notes: Table 1 (p.5, BBQ-Lite) + Table 4 (p.6, ablation) + Fig.3/4 (mistake-rate reduction, out-of-domain transfer) are load-bearing. Not RECONSIDERAR — a foundational negative-knowledge/rule-accumulation paper, squarely on-topic.

cita: Zheng, S., He, K., Yang, L. y Xiong, J. (2024). MemoryRepository for AI NPC.
problema: LLM-based game NPCs lack long-term, human-like memory: without persistent memory NPCs cannot recall past interactions, breaking narrative coherence, while simply keeping all history is infeasible under a hard token budget and does not resemble human forgetting/consolidation.
mecanismo: MemoryRepository splits each NPC's memory into a Short-Term Memory Room (full detail, capped at 10 dialogue turns) and a Long-Term Memory Room (compact summaries); a scheduling policy summarizes and forgets short-term entries into long-term memory in parallel (not sequentially) once the turn cap is reached under the fixed token budget T(P)+T(C)+T(M)<=T_limit; retrieval uses an Interactive Dual-Tower DSSM (ID-DSSM, a dual-encoder over dialogue-turn embeddings) with ANN indexing akin to FAISS to fetch the most relevant memory unit for the current turn.
evaluacion: A 400-question (200 LLM-generated + 200 human-authored) validation set is scored by human annotators on 4 metrics (memory retrieval accuracy, response correctness, contextual coherence, human-likeness) across GPT-4/GPT-3.5/ChatGLM with and without MemoryRepository, plus a head-to-head comparison against MemGPT at dialogue round 100, and a robustness sweep over temperature/top-p.
numeros_clave: At round 100, MemGPT vs MemoryRepository-embedded GPT-3.5: retrieval 0.831 vs 0.806, correctness 0.713 vs 0.705, coherence 0.874 vs 0.886, human-like 0.718 vs 0.861 (Table 3) — MemoryRepository trades a small retrieval/correctness cost for a large human-likeness gain; short-term room capped at 10 dialogue turns before forced summarization; the authors' own baseline comparison shows correctness roughly unchanged while retrieval DECLINES after adding the forgetting mechanism (§VI.B.1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The authors explicitly report that adding the forgetting/summarization mechanism does NOT improve correctness and DEGRADES the retrieval metric versus the no-memory baseline (§VI.B.1) — an honest, measured tradeoff (fidelity for human-likeness) rather than a hidden or glossed-over cost, which is itself the kind of negative/limitation finding MF values.

Summarization and forgetting are explicitly modeled as simultaneous, not sequential, processes — short-term entries are pruned AND distilled into long-term memory in the same pass once a fixed turn budget (10 turns) is reached (§III.C.2, Eq.2) — a concrete recency-triggered consolidation cadence MF could reference.

The whole architecture is explicitly derived from a hard token-budget constraint T(P)+T(C)+T(M)<=T_limit (Eq.1, §III.C) — memory tiering exists specifically to store more information without raising the token ceiling, directly matching MF's context-economy framing.

Retrieval quality is measured against a real competing system (MemGPT) at a fixed dialogue depth rather than assumed superior (Table 3, §VI.B.2), though the comparison is a single-round snapshot rather than a longitudinal ablation, limiting how strongly it can be read as MF's fuller measured-retrieval standard.

notes: Table 3 (p.11, MemGPT comparison) + §VI.B.1 (retrieval-degradation trade-off) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a direct long-term/human-like memory architecture paper for LLM agents.

cita: Ge, Y., Romeo, S., Cai, J., Shu, R., Benajiba, Y., Sunkara, M., & Zhang, Y. (2025). TReMu: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Temporal Reasoning for LLM-Agents with Memory in Multi-Session Dialogues.
problema: Temporal reasoning across multi-session dialogues is under-benchmarked and hard for LLM agents: relative-time expressions require inferring an event's true date separately from when it was mentioned, and cross-session dependencies require correctly relating events retrieved from different, possibly stale, sessions.
mecanismo: TReMu combines time-aware memorization (per-session timeline summarization that extracts events and infers their absolute dates, explicitly distinguishing occurrence-time from mention-time, then organizes memory as an indexed timeline) with neuro-symbolic reasoning (retrieved memory is fed to an LLM that generates executable Python code using datetime/dateutil plus custom helper functions like weekRange, as the reasoning rationale before answering).
evaluacion: A new multi-choice temporal-QA benchmark built by augmenting LoCoMo (3 question types: Temporal Anchoring/Precedence/Interval, plus unanswerable questions) is evaluated on GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini/GPT-3.5-Turbo against Standard Prompting, CoT, MemoChat, MemoChat+CoT and Timeline+CoT baselines, with an ablation isolating memory representation (Timeline vs MemoChat) from reasoning strategy (CoT vs neuro-symbolic code), plus a code-execution-failure-rate diagnostic.
numeros_clave: GPT-4o overall accuracy: Standard Prompting 29.83 -> CoT 61.67 -> TReMu 77.67 (Table 5); ablation isolates two independent gains: Timeline+CoT (71.50) over MemoChat+CoT (41.67) shows time-aware memorization alone adds ~30pp, and TReMu (77.67) over Timeline+CoT (71.50) shows neuro-symbolic reasoning adds a further ~6pp; unanswerable-question F1 20.84->64.42 on GPT-4o (SP vs TReMu, Table 5); memory mechanisms HURT GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini vs plain CoT but HELPED the shorter-context GPT-3.5-Turbo (§4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper measures, rather than assumes, WHEN memory augmentation helps: MemoChat/Timeline memory mechanisms underperform plain CoT for GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini (whose native context already fits the whole dialogue) but improve results for the shorter-context GPT-3.5-Turbo (§4.2) — a measured conditional/negative finding that memory augmentation is not a universal win, supporting MF's stance of validating a mechanism's value rather than assuming it.

Time-aware memorization writes fine-grained memory pieces that explicitly separate an event's inferred OCCURRENCE date from its MENTION date and organizes them into an indexed timeline rather than one holistic per-session summary (§3.2.1, Table 3 vs Table 4 examples) — a concrete consolidation schema (date-anchored granular facts vs. lossy holistic summary) MF could adopt for its own docs/gotcha memory.

Distinguishing 'when an event occurred' from 'when it was mentioned' (§3.2.1) is precisely a provenance/staleness discipline — the memory schema itself encodes freshness/anchor metadata, directly matching MF's FIDELIDAD concern.

Structuring memory as a timeline of dated, retrievable event summaries (rather than raw dialogue or an undated blob, §3.2.1) is a concrete typed-narrative memory representation, relevant to MF's TIER-DOCS emphasis on dated, structured truth over flat text.

notes: Table 5 (p.9, GPT-4o results + ablation) and §4.2 discussion (memory hurts sufficiently-large-context models but helps GPT-3.5) are the load-bearing findings. Not RECONSIDERAR — a direct memory + temporal-reasoning paper for multi-session dialogue agents.

cita: Ouyang et al. (2025). ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory.
problema: LLM agents in persistent, long-running roles fail to learn from accumulated interaction history, repeating past errors and discarding insights; prior agent memory designs mostly store raw trajectories or only successful routines, leaving lessons from failures largely unexploited.
mecanismo: ReasoningBank distills structured memory items (title/description/content) from BOTH successful and failed trajectories, using an LLM-as-a-judge (no ground truth) to label outcomes; retrieval is embedding-based top-k similarity search injected as system instructions; new items are consolidated back via a simple addition operation, forming a closed retrieve-extract-consolidate loop; memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) further scales this by generating multiple trajectories per task (parallel self-contrast or sequential self-refinement) to produce richer contrastive signal for higher-quality memory curation.
evaluacion: Evaluated on WebArena, Mind2Web (web navigation/generalization) and SWE-Bench-Verified (repo-level issue resolving) with Gemini-2.5-flash/pro and Claude-3.7-sonnet backbones, against No-Memory, Synapse (trajectory memory) and AWM (workflow/success-only memory) baselines, reporting success rate and interaction-step efficiency, plus MaTTS scaling curves.
numeros_clave: WebArena overall success-rate gains of +8.3/+7.2/+4.6 over no-memory across the 3 backbones (Table 1); up to 16% fewer interaction steps and up to 20% relative effectiveness improvement (Abstract); SWE-Bench-Verified resolve rate 34.2->38.8 (Gemini-2.5-flash) and 54.0->57.4 (Gemini-2.5-pro) vs no-memory (Table 2); on the cross-website 'Multi' WebArena subset, AWM (success-only memory) actually DEGRADES vs no-memory while ReasoningBank still gains +4.6 SR (§4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: ReasoningBank explicitly extracts memory items from FAILED trajectories too (via LLM-as-judge outcome labeling, no ground truth needed) rather than success-only routines, and this is shown to matter directly: on WebArena's cross-website 'Multi' subset, the success-only AWM baseline DEGRADES vs no-memory while ReasoningBank still gains +4.6 SR (§4.2, Table 1) — strong evidence that negative/failure knowledge is load-bearing for generalization, confirming MF's negative-knowledge stance.

Memory consolidation is a simple addition into a growing repository rather than complex merging (§3.2), and memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) shows that USING contrastive signal from multiple trajectories of the SAME task (self-contrast) to curate memory produces measurably better memory than treating each trajectory independently (§3.3, §4.3-4.4) — a concrete recipe for higher-quality consolidation MF could adopt when synthesizing recipes from repeated similar gotchas.

Writes are gated by an LLM-as-a-judge outcome signal (success/failure) rather than admitted unconditionally, and both branches (success->validated strategy, failure->counterfactual pitfall) are explicitly distilled with different extraction strategies (§3.2) — matches MF's stance that memory admission needs a judged trigger, not automatic accumulation.

Effectiveness AND efficiency (interaction steps) are both reported as first-class measured outcomes against multiple real baselines (trajectory-based Synapse, workflow-based AWM) across 3 different backbone LLMs (Table 1-3) rather than assuming memory helps — matches MF's measured-retrieval standard.

notes: Table 1 (p.7, WebArena) + Table 2 (SWE-Bench-Verified) + the AWM-degrades-on-Multi-subset finding (§4.2) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a leading reasoning-memory paper, squarely on-topic and highly relevant to MF's negative-knowledge/consolidation axes.

cita: Chen et al. (2026). HaluMem: Evaluating Hallucinations in Memory Systems of Agents.
problema: Memory systems for LLM agents frequently hallucinate (fabricate, error, conflict, omit) during storage and retrieval, but existing evaluation is end-to-end question answering only, making it impossible to localize WHICH operational stage (extraction, updating, or answering) a given hallucination originates from.
mecanismo: HaluMem defines per-stage gold standards on a synthetic, six-stage-constructed, user-centered multi-turn dialogue dataset (persona -> life skeleton -> event flow -> session summaries/memory points -> full sessions -> questions): an extraction gold set of memory points that should be newly added, an updating gold set of old->new memory pairs, and a QA gold-answer set; each stage is scored independently (extraction: recall/weighted-recall/target-precision/accuracy/false-memory-resistance/F1; updating: correct-rate/hallucination-rate/omission-rate; QA: correct-rate/hallucination-rate/omission-rate) against 6 production memory systems (Mem0, Mem0-Graph, Memobase, MemOS, Supermemory, Zep).
evaluacion: Two benchmarks, HaluMem-Medium (about 15k memory points, 3.5k questions, avg 1.5k turns per user, up to 1M-token context) and HaluMem-Long (avg 2.6k turns per user, context exceeding 1M tokens with injected irrelevant dialogue), evaluated against 6 real production memory systems, plus a per-stage runtime/efficiency measurement.
numeros_clave: Extraction: all systems (except MemOS) show recall below 60% and accuracy below 62% on HaluMem-Medium (Table 3); memory-updating omission rates above 50% for most systems despite hallucination rates below 2% (few samples reach the update stage at all); QA answer accuracy below 70% for every system, degrading further on HaluMem-Long; dialogue-addition (write) time for Mem0/Mem0-Graph exceeds 2700 minutes on HaluMem-Medium, dwarfing retrieval time (Table 5) — write, not retrieval, is the computational bottleneck.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper's central methodological move is refusing end-to-end-only evaluation and instead localizing hallucinations to the exact operational stage (extraction vs. updating vs. QA), revealing that errors are generated and ACCUMULATE upstream (extraction/updating) then propagate downstream (Abstract, §6.2.1) — direct support for MF's stance that failures must be attributed to a specific stage/mechanism, not just observed in aggregate output.

Every production memory system tested (Mem0, Mem0-Graph, Memobase, MemOS, Supermemory) shows extraction accuracy below 62% and QA accuracy below 70%, with updating omission rates above 50% (Table 3, p.11) — hard quantitative evidence that today's real memory systems are riddled with fabrication/staleness/omission, squarely validating MF's FIDELIDAD concern as an urgent, measured problem rather than a theoretical one.

Runtime measurement shows the WRITE stage (dialogue ingestion/extraction), not retrieval, is the dominant computational cost — dialogue-addition time for Mem0/Mem0-Graph exceeds 2700 minutes on HaluMem-Medium (Table 5, §6.2.4) — confirms MF's context-economy concern should weight write-time cost, not just retrieval-time cost.

Memory updating performance is shown to be bottlenecked by extraction coverage — when a pre-update memory was never extracted, the corresponding update cannot be processed at all (§6.2.1) — a concrete causal chain (admission-gate quality gates downstream consolidation quality) relevant to MF's write-trigger design.

notes: Table 3 (p.11, per-stage hallucination results) + Table 5 (write-time bottleneck) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a rigorous operation-level hallucination benchmark directly on MF's FIDELIDAD axis, evaluating today's real production memory systems (Mem0, MemOS, Zep, etc.).

cita: Lindenbauer et al. (2025). From Knowledge to Noise: CTIM-Rover and the Pitfalls of Episodic Memory in Software Engineering Agents.
problema: Software-engineering agents (AutoCodeRover, SWE-agent) discard their episodic memory after each task instance, wasting cross-task learning opportunities; it is unclear whether an experiential-learning memory (ExpeL-style) that worked on simpler domains (QA, web shopping, ALFWorld) also transfers to the more complex, repository-level structure of real-world SE bug-fixing.
mecanismo: CTIM-Rover augments AutoCodeRover with a Mixture-of-Experts-inspired Cross-Task-Instance Memory: it collects successful (and self-reflected failure-to-success) trajectories, distills general SE knowledge and then repository-specific knowledge via an LLM (o1) in a two-phase pipeline (add/edit/upvote/downvote operations from ExpeL), caps the memory at sqrt(n) items, and separately supports exemplar retrieval of the single most similar past successful trajectory (Code-T5 embeddings, cosine similarity >=90% threshold) injected once at the start of the agent's trajectory.
evaluacion: Evaluated on a 45-sample held-out subset of SWE-bench Verified against baseline AutoCodeRover across 6 configurations (full CTIM-Rover, CTIM-only, general-CTIM-only, repo-level-CTIM-only, exemplar-only), reporting per-repository and overall success rate (Table 1), plus a manual qualitative trace analysis of two solved-by-baseline-but-failed-by-CTIM instances.
numeros_clave: Overall success rate: AutoCodeRover baseline 42% vs full CTIM-Rover 40% (-2pp) vs CTIM-only 31% (-11pp) vs repo-level-CTIM-only 31% vs exemplar-only 40% (Table 1, 45 samples); qualitative trace analysis shows a SINGLE repository-level CTIM sentence containing the word 'clean' biased the agent away from the correct patch location (django-13933); removing that one item, or even inserting an arbitrary unrelated string ('GRANDMA LIKES PASTA'), restored the correct solve on a second case (django-15987), directly demonstrating noise-not-signal causation (§5.1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: This paper's negative result IS the load-bearing finding MF's NEGATIVO axis cares about: a plausible experiential-memory mechanism was tested and shown, via controlled ablation plus causal tracing, to actively HURT (not just fail to help) — a single noisy CTIM sentence flips a correct solve to incorrect (§5.1) — exactly the kind of documented, causally-traced negative result MF wants captured as durable knowledge, not silently discarded.

The paper's own proposed remedy — embedding-based, task-similar retrieval instead of showing the full undifferentiated CTIM — is left untested (§6 Limitations) even though the diagnosed cause is exactly a retrieval/filtering failure (irrelevant items always injected); this is a partial REFUTA of 'just add a memory index' as sufficient: more knowledge without a working relevance filter is shown to be net-negative, cautioning MF against assuming a derived index alone (without gating) is safe.

Memory items are admitted from successful trajectories (plus self-reflected failure-to-success tuples) via an ExpeL-style add/edit/upvote/downvote knowledge-distillation pipeline (§4.1), yet even this curated admission process was not enough to prevent noise from degrading performance — evidence that MF's write-trigger gating must also account for DOWNSTREAM interference, not just admission quality.

The paper isolates exactly which mechanism causes the harm via a systematic 6-configuration ablation (Table 1) plus manual causal tracing of individual CTIM items to specific wrong actions (§5.1) rather than reporting only an aggregate score — a rigorous measured-retrieval methodology matching MF's G-M2 standard.

notes: Table 1 (p.4, 6-configuration ablation) + §5.1 qualitative causal-tracing case studies (p.4-5, the 'clean' and 'GRANDMA LIKES PASTA' cases) are the load-bearing evidence. Not RECONSIDERAR — a rigorous, well-isolated negative-result paper on episodic memory for SE agents, high-value for MF's NEGATIVO/anti-poisoning stance.
